title: Hypothesis tests, multiplicity and temporal leakage

objectives.text: Interpret a predeclared exact test and apply a Bonferroni familywise bound without confusing p-values, effect size or post-selection evidence.
Enforce point-in-time feature and training-label availability, keeping preprocessing and model choice out of the final evaluation data.

blocks.markdown: A test starts with a specified null model, alternative, statistic, sampling/stopping rule and decision threshold. A p-value is a tail probability of the observed-or-more-extreme statistic UNDER that null model and its assumptions. It is not P(null is true), the chance the result was caused by chance alone, the size of an effect, or a trading instruction. Not rejecting a null does not establish that it is true; rejecting can reflect an incorrect null or other violated model assumptions.

Synthetic example: fix n=8 independent binary trials in advance, null success probability 1/2, and the one-sided alternative p>1/2. The statistic K is the success count; larger is more extreme. For observed K=7, the exact right-tail p-value is P0(K≥7)=C(8,7)/256+C(8,8)/256=9/256. The tail direction was not chosen after seeing the result. A two-sided alternative needs its own predeclared extremeness rule; this helper implements only the stated one-sided tail.

blocks.source:
from fractions import Fraction
from math import comb

def binomial_right_tail(n, observed, null_p):
    if type(n) is not int or not 0 <= n <= 50 or type(observed) is not int or not 0 <= observed <= n:
        raise ValueError("expected integer n in [0,50] and observed in [0,n]")
    if type(null_p) is not Fraction or not 0 <= null_p <= 1:
        raise ValueError("expected Fraction null probability in [0,1]")
    return sum((comb(n,k)*null_p**k*(1-null_p)**(n-k)
                for k in range(observed,n+1)), Fraction(0))

p_value = binomial_right_tail(8, 7, Fraction(1,2))
alpha = Fraction(1,20)
family_size = 20
print(p_value)
print(p_value <= alpha)
print(alpha / family_size)
print(p_value <= alpha / family_size)
print(min(Fraction(1), family_size*p_value))
blocks.caption: Expected output: 9/256, True, 1/400, False, then 45/64. At α=1/20 the predeclared single test crosses its threshold. For a complete family of 20 valid tests, α/20=1/400; this p-value does not cross that Bonferroni threshold. Multiplying by 20 and capping at 1 gives its Bonferroni-adjusted p-value, not a posterior probability.

blocks.markdown: If m tests each have a valid null rejection probability at most α/m, the union bound gives P(at least one false rejection)≤Σ_(true nulls)P(reject that null)≤m*(α/m)=α. This Bonferroni familywise guarantee does not require independence between tests, but it DOES require valid individual test procedures and a correctly defined family. Within-test dependence or unplanned optional stopping that invalidates an individual p-value is not repaired by multiplication. The bound may be conservative and lower power; it is not a promise of exactly α false findings.

The family can include many features, horizons, parameter choices, subgroup analyses and repeated looks, not merely the one result printed in a final report. Reporting only the smallest p-value hides this selection. Record all attempted comparisons and stopping decisions. Reusing a final holdout to choose the winning model turns it into development data; a correction based on a conveniently smaller family does not restore an untouched evaluation. Preplanned sequential or selective methods exist, but are not implemented here.

For a prediction decided at time d, a feature must have been available no later than d, not merely describe an earlier event. A future label can become available after d, but it cannot train a model before its label-availability time. The metadata helper defines an explicit frozen fit snapshot at t: training decisions must be strictly before t and labels available by t; final evaluation decisions must be strictly after t. Equal-time decisions are excluded by this policy to avoid implying that fitting and prediction happen simultaneously.

blocks.title: Event order alone is not enough

steps.text: At the frozen fit cutoff t=15, A has decision 10 and label available 13, so it can train.
B has decision 11 but label available 18. Its early decision does not make the future outcome known at fitting; exclude it from training.
C has decision 16, after the snapshot, and D has decision 15 exactly at it. Neither belongs to this strict-before training policy.
A feature available at 12 for a decision at 10 is a contract error, even if its original event timestamp was earlier.

blocks.caption: Expected output: ['A'], then future feature rejected. Integer timestamps are synthetic shared-clock units, not a timezone parser. Rows identify a future-outcome task; label_available must be at or after its decision. All row metadata is validated before a result is returned, and input order is preserved. This is an eligibility example, not a complete purged walk-forward splitter.

blocks.markdown: Split before learning any transformation: imputation values, centering/scaling, feature selection and model parameters must be fitted within the training fold. Apply that frozen transformation to later validation/test rows. For train values [1,3] and held-out value 100, training mean 2 gives held-out centered value 98. Using all three values gives mean 104/3 and leaks the held-out distribution into the transform. A pipeline helps maintain this boundary, but cannot fix incorrectly timestamped source features.

Chronological row order alone does not guarantee clean evaluation: overlapping target windows, duplicated entities, delayed revisions and labels that cross fold boundaries can share information. Define event/feature/label availability and the full outcome interval, then choose exclusions or a gap appropriate to that task. A gap counted in rows is not automatically a fixed time duration on irregular data. The referenced TimeSeriesSplit is not executed here and does not by itself infer label-window or revision semantics.

Independent transfer: compute the exact right-tail p-value for 8 successes in 8 trials and compare it with α/20, preserving the original one-sided null. Then design a timeline with one late label and one late feature: state which is temporarily ineligible and which violates a prediction-time contract. Describe train/validation/final-test roles and list every transformation learned before evaluation. Explain what new untouched evidence would be needed after tuning on a former test set.

References: [ASA p-value principles](https://www.amstat.org/asa/files/pdfs/P-ValueStatement.pdf), [NIST Bonferroni inequality](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/prc/section4/prc473.htm), [scikit-learn leakage guidance](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html) and [TimeSeriesSplit contract](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.TimeSeriesSplit.html). Only standard-library synthetic code is executed; no scikit-learn capability or live-data validation is implied.

summary: A p-value is conditional on a test model, not the probability a hypothesis is true. Multiplicity needs a complete family and valid tests. Evaluation must respect availability, training-only transformations and genuinely untouched outcomes.
